part_of_speech: adjective (used as noun of address), feminine singular
etymology: From Old French mignon, possibly from Gaulish or Germanic roots meaning 'delicate' or 'favorite', popularized in courtly and amorous contexts during the Renaissance.
in_context: Functions as a vocative noun of address, establishing an intimate, affectionate tone toward the addressee (traditionally a young woman) whom the speaker invites to observe the rose.
